name: Plus Power
headquarters: The Woodlands (Houston), Texas, United States (founded San Francisco; HQ moved Jul 2023)
ownership: private — founders/management + undisclosed institutional investors (~$315M equity raised per PitchBook, which also names OMERS Private Equity — unverified by any first-party or news source); PE Hub reported sale interest in Jan 2024 with no completed process found through Aug 2026
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Plus Power is the most bankability-obsessed standalone-storage specialist in the US — 9 operating facilities, 1,650 MW / 4,150 MWh across AZ, HI, MA, ME and TX, an 11+ GW pipeline, and more than $2.5B of disclosed project capital raised through five different tax-equity/debt syndicates. It is a proven DUAL-SOURCE buyer, split per-project between Tesla Megapack (Kapolei HI — 158 units; Sierra Estrella + Superstition AZ — marketed as US-made; Cranberry Point MA) and Sungrow PowerTitan (the ERCOT trio; Cross Town ME — 156 units), with 330+ Sungrow containers deployed through 2025 CODs and no public FEOC posture statement anywhere — the single biggest intel hole on the account. No Hithium contact exists. Its AIDC hook is the sharpest in the batch outside Eolian: Sierra Estrella (250 MW/1,000 MWh, SRP tolling) is explicitly marketed as grid support for the adjacent Prime Data Centers 240 MW hyperscale campus in Avondale, AZ, and Laurel Creek (250 MW/1,000 MWh, 2029) sits at a critical AEP substation in data-center-alley PJM.
ecosystemRole: We assess Plus Power as the utility-tolling franchise of the standalone-storage tier: one new 20-year tolling market per year (Hawaiian Electric → SRP → PNM → TVA), the two largest batteries in New England, a seasoned 700 MW ERCOT merchant fleet, and grid-forming firsts (Kapolei's synthetic inertia/black-start flagship replaced an AES coal plant). For the relationship web it demonstrates the buying pattern Hithium must beat: integrated systems purchased from exactly two suppliers chosen per-project on bankability and geography, financed through tax-equity syndicates (Morgan Stanley, BofA, Foss, Greenprint) whose diligence any new OEM must clear. Its near-term procurement window is Corazon (150 MW/600 MWh, PNM 20-yr toll, construction 2026) — squarely inside the FEOC-constrained vintage — with Crawfish Creek (TVA, 2028 build) and Laurel Creek (2029) behind it.

productsAndServices.name: Contracted utility fleet (the tolling franchise)
productsAndServices.description: Kapolei (KES), Oahu — 185 MW/565 MWh, online Dec 2023/Jan 2024, 20-yr ESA with Hawaiian Electric; replaces AES coal; grid-forming with synthetic inertia, black start, 50 MW/25 MWh fast-frequency response at 250 ms ('world's most advanced BESS' — company-claimed). Sierra Estrella, Avondale AZ — 250 MW/1,000 MWh, and Superstition, Gilbert AZ — 90 MW/360 MWh, both COD Jun 2024 under 20-yr SRP tolling. Corazon, Albuquerque NM — 150 MW/600 MWh, 20-yr PNM tolling (awarded Nov 2024), construction 2026, COD late 2027. Crawfish Creek, Jackson Co. AL — 200 MW/800 MWh, 20-yr TVA ESA (Apr 2026), construction 2028, COD summer 2029.
productsAndServices.positioning: The heaviest publicized use of 20-year utility tolling structures among the standalone peer set — one new tolling market per year since 2021.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term utility ESAs/tolls; tax equity (Morgan Stanley, BofA, Foss & Co., Greenprint) + multi-bank debt syndicates.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utilities with retiring thermal capacity and data-center-driven load growth (SRP, TVA, PNM, Hawaiian Electric).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Corazon equipment procurement is effectively NOW (2026 construction start); TVA/Southeast entry (7th state) opens a new franchise.

productsAndServices.name: Merchant & capacity fleet (ERCOT + ISO-NE)
productsAndServices.description: ERCOT trio (all COD Dec 2023-Jun 2024): Rodeo Ranch, Pecos — 300 MW/600 MWh (merchant + Goldman Sachs commodities hedge on a portion; largest operating standalone ERCOT BESS at COD); Ebony, Comal Co. — 200 MW/400 MWh; Anemoi, Edinburg — 200 MW/400 MWh. ISO-NE pair: Cranberry Point, Carver MA — 150 MW/300 MWh (online May 2025; largest BESS in New England at announcement); Cross Town, Gorham ME — 175 MW/350 MWh (operational Nov 2025, inaugurated Feb 2026 — now the largest BESS on the ISO-NE grid; 7-yr capacity contract from the 2021 FCA; claimed 100% availability through Winter Storm Fern). Heritage: developed Gambit (100 MW, Angleton TX), sold to Tesla in 2021; Bat Cave and North Fork sold to Broad Reach in 2020.
productsAndServices.positioning: First-mover in ISO-NE standalone storage (2021 FCA wins) — the two largest batteries in New England are both Plus Power's; the ERCOT fleet is a seasoned merchant cash generator.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Merchant with selective hedges (Goldman), ISO-NE capacity contracts + ITC monetization.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 11+ GW development pipeline across 20+ states (company-claimed; a 2024 variant said 10 GW across 28 states and Canada).

productsAndServices.name: Procurement model (dual-source: Tesla + Sungrow)
productsAndServices.description: Per-project supplier split confirmed by then-CEO Keefe (Nov 2023): 'Texas projects used Sungrow, Arizona used Tesla.' Verified pairings — Tesla Megapack: Kapolei (158 Megapack 2 XL), Sierra Estrella (276 units, 'designed and manufactured in the US' per SRP), Superstition, Cranberry Point (82 Megapack 2XL per Mass DPU filings). Sungrow PowerTitan: Ebony (176 containers), Cross Town (156 units), Rodeo Ranch/Anemoi (interview-attributed). By Nov 2022 the company had secured 6.5 GWh of battery supply for projects through 2025+ and was reselling near-term excess to other developers (supplier split undisclosed). EPCs: Gridworks (all three ERCOT projects), Sturgeon Electric (Sierra Estrella), Cianbro (Cross Town); in-house EPC organization under SVP Edgar Nunez.
productsAndServices.positioning: No exclusive integrator lock — but deep Tesla institutional ties (Exec Vice Chairman Bobby Rudd and CDO Molly Emerson are Tesla/SolarCity alumni; the Gambit sale went to Tesla) and >330 Sungrow containers of installed-base familiarity form high switching inertia on both flanks.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct integrated-system purchases; no direct cell-level procurement disclosed (cells arrive via Tesla and Sungrow).
productsAndServices.roadmap: No public FEOC/domestic-content strategy statement located anywhere — the biggest open question, since Corazon (2026 build), Crawfish (2028) and Laurel Creek (2029) all sit in FEOC-governed vintages and the incumbent Sungrow faces the same disqualification math as any Chinese supplier.

productsAndServices.name: AIDC adjacency (grid-side, not behind-the-meter)
productsAndServices.description: Sierra Estrella is explicitly marketed as 'critical grid infrastructure to support the adjacent Prime Data Center campus' — Prime Data Centers' $3B, 240 MW, 5-building hyperscale campus in Avondale, AZ (broke ground May 21, 2026). Laurel Creek (VA, AEP/PJM, 250 MW/1,000 MWh, 2029) sits 'at a critical AEP grid substation' in the national data-center epicenter. The TVA deal is framed around Southeast demand growth that is heavily data-center-driven.
productsAndServices.positioning: A grid-side beneficiary of AI load growth rather than a behind-the-meter data-center supplier — no hyperscaler offtake, no co-location contracts, no dedicated data-center product line found.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utilities serving hyperscale campuses (SRP/Avondale; AEP/Virginia; TVA/Southeast).
productsAndServices.roadmap: The fleet increasingly sits where AI load lands — the AIDC thesis expresses through siting and utility demand, not named tech counterparties.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Plus Power as a genuinely open dual-source buyer historically — Tesla and Sungrow split the fleet per-project — which cuts both ways for Hithium: the account demonstrably buys Chinese integrated systems at scale (330+ Sungrow containers through 2025), but displacement now requires beating BOTH an entrenched US-made incumbent with deep alumni ties AND an installed-base Chinese incumbent, under FEOC rules that burden any Chinese entrant equally.

(High confidence) We assess the absence of any public FEOC/domestic-content posture as the account's defining intel gap: no executive statement, no safe-harbor disclosure, no 2025 equipment pre-buy evidence — yet Corazon's 2026 construction start forces the question immediately. Primary-contact discovery on how Plus Power intends to keep the 30% ITC on 2026+ vintages is the first sales-intelligence task.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the bankability gauntlet as the practical qualification bar: five tax-equity/debt syndicates (Morgan Stanley, BofA, Foss, Greenprint + bank clubs) and an independent-engineer process every supplier must clear — a well-capitalized Hithium with Mesquite assembly and long warranties can plausibly pass the technical/financial screens, but the FEOC tax math and NDAA §154 optics (military-adjacent Kapolei marketing; red-state utility counterparties TVA/SRP) are the harder walls.

(Moderate confidence) We assess near-term volume as thin and long-cycle: only Corazon (600 MWh) is imminent; Crawfish (800 MWh) builds 2028 and Laurel Creek (1,000 MWh) targets 2029 — against an 11+ GW paper pipeline of uncertain conversion. The realistic Hithium play is positioning for the 2027-2029 procurement cycle with a FEOC-compliant offering, while tracking the unresolved ownership question (a sale could reset supplier policy).

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: Plus Power is the best evidence that utility tolling — not merchant ERCOT — is where standalone storage economics are heading (five 20-year tolls across four utilities), and utility counterparties bring procurement scrutiny that favors domestic content. Watch whether the Sungrow relationship survives FEOC as the leading indicator of whether ANY Chinese-brand system retains a path at this account.
